# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [9]
LIGHT [red]
STRIP painted [green] [yellow] [yellow]
KEYPAD engraved 1:[1] 2:[5] 3:[2] 4:[8] [1 digits] [entered nothing]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[white] 3:[blue] 4:[red] 5:[purple] 6:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ ✌ 🤟]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👎]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👋 👍]

My position: I am the only one who sees the bomb, and the only one who cannot hear. Working out who connects to whom: Mute can hear me speak; Blind can hear me speak too (only the table's Deaf row bars hearing); my gestures reach Mute only. Nobody can reach Mute→Blind directly — Mute's gestures are invisible to Blind and Mute cannot talk — so I am the relay: Mute signs to me, I speak to Blind. That makes my first job clear: put the entire visual read-out into words, out loud, so both hearers hold it.

What arrived for me: Mute sent what reads like "1, 2, 3" — probably counting or asking me to report the first parts — and "thumbs up, thumbs down", almost certainly offering a yes/no channel, which works because Mute can hear my replies. Blind sent a wave and a thumbs-up: a hello and a check that I'm alive; since Blind cannot see my gestures at all, the only way back to Blind is my voice.

The read-out I hold: display 9; light red; strip green-yellow-yellow; keypad keys 1/5/2/8 with a strange status ("one digit", "entered nothing" — I'll report it verbatim and let the manual decide what it means); six wires yellow, white, blue, red, purple, green. I'll extend Mute's obvious finger-counting into a module code, confirm contact with a thumbs-up, and ask Blind to pour out the tactile half of the bomb — which I cannot see and Mute cannot touch.

```
speak(text="Can you hear me? I am Deaf: I see the bomb, I hear nothing, I can talk. Full read-out. Display shows 9. Light is red. Strip painted, in order: green, yellow, yellow. Keypad: four keys engraved 1, 5, 2, 8 - key one is 1, key two is 5, key three is 2, key four is 8. Its status reads, exactly as printed: one digit, entered nothing. Wires, six in a row: one yellow, two white, three blue, four red, five purple, six green. That is every colour and mark on the bomb. Blind: I received your wave, yes. Tell me everything you feel - the order of the wires under your fingers, whether the keys click differently, any ridges or braille - by voice if you can speak, otherwise gesture to me and I will say it aloud.")
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, your signs arrived. Code proposal: thumbs up means yes, thumbs down means no; I answer by voice, since you can hear me. To have me read out a part, show me its number: one finger is the display, two fingers the light, three fingers the strip, crossed fingers the keypad, open hand the wires. When you know what Blind must do, gesture the steps to me and I will relay them word for word to Blind, who cannot see your hands.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍"])
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [3]
LIGHT [yellow]
STRIP painted [green] [yellow] [yellow]
KEYPAD engraved 1:[1] 2:[5] 3:[2] 4:[8] [1 digits] [entered nothing]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[white] 3:[blue] 4:[red] 5:[purple] 6:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✋ 🖐 👋 🤟 🖖 🤝]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [✊ 🖖 ✊ 🤚 👍]

New facts first: between rounds the display fell from 9 to 3 and the light went red to yellow. Nothing else moved, and the keypad status is unchanged — so this smells like a countdown, which makes speed my top priority. I also need to fix an error I made last turn: I told Blind to answer by voice, but I am Deaf — Blind's speech can never reach me. Blind's only channel to me is gesture, and since Blind can't see, the code must be built from shapes Blind can feel on their own hand: finger counts, fist, thumbs. Mute's signs I read as open-hands (my code: wires / five), then three, four, handshake — plausibly "wires: three and four, agreed", perhaps red light→3, yellow light→4, which would be live right now since the light just turned yellow. But I will not relay an unverified wire instruction to Blind — a wrong cut is fatal. I confirm the decode with Mute first, demand the manual's word on the countdown, and give Blind the felt-shape code plus an urgent question about whether they touched anything.

```
speak(text="Urgent update for both of you: since last round the display dropped from 9 to 3 and the light changed red to yellow. Everything else is identical - strip green yellow yellow, keypad engraved 1 5 2 8 still reading one digit, entered nothing, wires still yellow white blue red purple green. If that display is a countdown we may be short on time. Mute, the manual is our clock - check it first.")
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, your signs reached me as: open hand, open hand, wave, three, four, handshake. My best guess: wires module, three and four, agreed - for example red light means cut wire three, yellow light means cut wire four. Do not make me act on a guess. Answer with thumbs up if that reading is right, thumbs down if wrong, then resend cleanly using only this code: thumbs up yes, thumbs down no; one finger display, two fingers light, three fingers strip, four fingers keypad, five fingers wires; numbers by finger count. Three questions, in order of urgency. One: what does the manual say the display does - is it a countdown, and what happens at zero? Two: what does the light colour mean, red versus yellow? Three: does the strip green yellow yellow appear in any rule? And when you know what Blind must do, phrase it as one short instruction and I will relay it to Blind word for word - remember Blind cannot see your hands and Blind cannot be reached by you directly, only through my voice.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, correction to my last message, this is important: I am Deaf. Your voice never reaches me, nobody's voice does. The only thing I can receive from you is your gestures. So use gestures, and use ones you can feel on your own hand. Code: a fist means zero or none. Extend fingers to count - one finger is one, two is two, three is three, four is four, a flat open hand is five. Thumbs up yes, thumbs down no. Answer these in order. First, thumbs up or down: did you touch or press anything on the bomb between my last message and now? The display fell from 9 to 3 and the light turned from red to yellow, so if that was you I must know exactly what you did. Second, count with fingers: how many keys are on the keypad under your hand, and do all the keys feel identical? Third: the six wires - sweep them with one finger left to right and tell me anything you can feel that distinguishes them: thickness, texture, ridges. Fourth: is there anything under your hands I cannot see - braille, switches, a panel seam, anything that moves or clicks?")
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [2]
LIGHT [red]
STRIP painted [green] [yellow] [yellow]
KEYPAD engraved 1:[1] 2:[5] 3:[2] 4:[8] [1 digits] [entered nothing]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[white] 3:[blue] 4:[red] 5:[purple] 6:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎 👎 👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🖐]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🖐 🤟 🖖]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👋 👎 🖖 👎 ✍ ✊ ✍ ☝ ✌ ☝ ✊ 👍]

The decode is coming together. Mute answered in order: thumbs down to my guess, then a triple thumbs down, then — five (wires), five-three-four (wires: 3, 4), thumbs up. So my red→3/yellow→4 theory was wrong, and the actual manual instruction, now confirmed twice, is: wires, cut 3 and 4. The earlier 👎👎👎 likely answers my three questions (display: no rule, light: no rule, strip: no rule) — the wires module is the whole game. Blind's message opens with wave + thumbs down: they touched nothing, so the display drop (now 9→3→2, accelerating toward zero) is an autonomous countdown. Then Blind improvised — writing-hand, fist, "1 2 1", fist, yes — probably tactile detail about engravings or keys; I'll re-query with tighter yes/no questions rather than guess. The critical move: Blind's report of nothing-touched means nobody has acted yet, the clock is at 2, and my messages land on Blind before their next action — so I must relay the cut instruction NOW, with a safeguard, and demand Mute pin down order and timing in parallel. One comfort: "cut wires 3 and 4" is the middle pair of six, identical counted from either end, so Blind's orientation can't be wrong about which two.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, urgent - act on this the moment you receive it. The manual's instruction, relayed through Mute and confirmed: cut wire three, then wire four. You know there are six wires in a row. The targets are the two middle wires, third and fourth from the end - the same pair counted from either end, so it does not matter which end you call first. Cut the third wire. If the bomb has not detonated, cut the fourth wire. Then thumbs up. If what you feel contradicts me - not six wires in a row, no way to cut - stop, make a fist, and gesture me. The display is a countdown sitting at 2, so do not wait for more messages from me. While you work, three answers by gesture, in this order. One, thumbs up or down: do the four keypad keys have raised engraving or braille you can feel? Two, finger count: how many digits does the keypad feel like it has registered? Three, thumbs up or down: after the second cut, does anything change under your hands - light warmth, a click, movement?")
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, I decoded you as: my red-yellow guess wrong, instruction is wires three and four, confirmed yes. I have already relayed to Blind: cut the third wire, then the fourth. Answer with single thumbs, one question per message, in this order. One: is cutting BOTH wires three and four correct - up or down? Two: does the ORDER of the two cuts matter - up if yes, down if no? Three: does the light colour or the display number control WHEN to cut, or is now fine - up if now, down if must wait? Four: the keypad status says one digit, entered nothing - does the manual require entering a digit before or after the cuts, and if yes, finger-count which engraved key? Five: what happens when the display reaches zero? If any part of my relay to Blind is wrong, thumbs down plus finger-counted correction immediately - Blind acts next turn and the display is at 2.")
```
